translationRepairs: Taizu marched north to Cang, then wheeled the army back on the capital.
Taizu marched north to Chan, then wheeled the army back on the capital.
Chinese 至澶州 names Chanzhou (Chan); Cang would be 滄州. The proposed Chan restores the correct place without other changes.
Taizu led troops north, reached Cang prefecture, then turned the army toward the capital.
Taizu led troops north, reached Chan prefecture, then turned the army toward the capital.
Literal 至澶州 is Chan prefecture, not Cang prefecture; the replacement corrects only that misreading.
He sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhang from Wuling toward Jiang to meet Jun.
He sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhao from Wuling toward Jiang to meet Jun.
康延沼 ends in 沼 (zhǎo), so Yanzhao; Yanzhang would require 章. The rest of the sentence is unchanged and matches 陳思讓、康延沼.
Separately he sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhang out from Wuling toward Jiang prefecture to join Jun.
Separately he sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhao out from Wuling toward Jiang prefecture to join Jun.
Same name error in the literal: 康延沼 is Kang Yanzhao, not Yanzhang.
Khitan raids brought Yin with troops to Cang.
Khitan raids brought Yin with troops to Chan.
屯澶州 is Chan, not Cang; the repair corrects the place-name only.
When the Khitan raided the border, Han sent Yin with troops to garrison at Cang.
When the Khitan raided the border, Han sent Yin with troops to garrison at Chan.
Literal garrison at 澶州 must be Chan, not Cang.
The Hidden Emperor had killed Yang Bin and others and ordered Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Cang and Guo Chong to kill Taizu at Wei.
The Hidden Emperor had killed Yang Bin and others and ordered Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Chan and Guo Chong to kill Taizu at Wei.
殺殷於澶州 places the ordered killing at Chan; Cang is the wrong prefecture name.
The Hidden Emperor had already killed Yang Bin and others; he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Cang, and also ordered Guo Chong to kill Zhou Taizu at Wei.
The Hidden Emperor had already killed Yang Bin and others; he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Chan, and also ordered Guo Chong to kill Zhou Taizu at Wei.
Literal 於澶州 is at Chan; replacing Cang with Chan fixes the place without altering agents or other facts.
The edict reached Cang. Hongyi feared failure and warned Yin. Yin sent a rider to Wei; Taizu rose in revolt.
The edict reached Chan. Hongyi feared failure and warned Yin. Yin sent a rider to Wei; Taizu rose in revolt.
詔書至澶州 means the edict reached Chan; Cang is incorrect.
When the edict reached Cang, Hongyi feared the affair would fail and instead told Yin. Yin sent a man galloping to Wei to inform Zhou Taizu, and they then raised troops in revolt.
When the edict reached Chan, Hongyi feared the affair would fail and instead told Yin. Yin sent a man galloping to Wei to inform Zhou Taizu, and they then raised troops in revolt.
Literal 至澶州 is Chan; the rest of the sentence already matches 弘義…告殷 and the revolt with Taizu.
Shu men captured with Huan Shizong spared and kept in the ranks. Many later fled south to Jing, yet Shizong trusted Huan all the more.
Shu men captured with Huan, Shizong spared and kept in the ranks. Many later fled south to Jing, yet Shizong trusted Huan all the more.
與環俱擒者，世宗不殺 separates those captured with Huan from Shizong as agent; without the comma, English fuses “Huan Shizong.” The proposed comma restores that split without inventing content.
